# ARD: One G-code generator banner

## Decision

Whenever Ares emits a G-code generator banner, write exactly this line, followed by a newline:

```text
; generated by OrcaSlicer Ares-<CARGO_PKG_VERSION> on 1980-01-01 at 00:00:00
```

`<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` is the Ares package version, not the upstream compatibility version. Plain G-code and G-code embedded in a sliced 3MF use the same banner. `OrcaSlicer` identifies the slicer family, and `Ares-<version>` identifies the producer and its version while retaining the `generated by OrcaSlicer` substring used by compatible viewers. The fixed timestamp remains unchanged.

## Upstream boundary

OrcaSlicer v2.5.0 (`40ecc66f78ed72dc368e0c1ebe40d77f00cc8a19`) emits the generator comment in `src/libslic3r/GCode.cpp:4242`. In `src/libslic3r/GCode/GCodeProcessor.cpp`, the `Producers` table includes `generated by OrcaSlicer` (2748–2754), and `GCodeProcessor::detect_producer` searches for that text as a substring (5164–5175). This classification lets the OrcaSlicer/BambuStudio viewer load the G-code configuration block (3886–3894) and honor `;HEIGHT` and `;WIDTH` comments when producer detection is enabled (4579–4590).

In `ares-core`, `gcode_header.rs` and the archive both use the generator text from `project_slice/gcode_emit/header.rs`. Change only that shared producer text. Keep the existing header placement and suppression rules and compute the archive plate MD5 from the emitted G-code bytes as before. Do not change slicing, tag emission, configuration payloads, archive layout, or WASM API version reporting.

## Verification

- Exercise the public export paths and check the exact Ares banner in plain and embedded G-code, including its version and timestamp.
- For the sliced 3MF comparison, first check each archive's stored plate MD5 against its own raw uncompressed G-code. Normalize only the generator comment in the comparison copies (producer text and timestamp), then recompute the corresponding plate MD5 from each normalized payload. Keep the rest of the G-code and archive comparison unchanged. This supersedes the timestamp-only comparison and distinct standalone label in [the sliced 3MF spec](cli-export-3mf-sliced.md#exact-comparison).
- Update exact Ares banner handling in Rust and desktop web tests; leave general generator patterns and the `orca_parity.rs` test root unchanged. Compare the affected official and seeded Orca parity families and the affected desktop web tests before and after the change, with no passing case becoming a failure. Also run formatting, workspace Clippy for all targets, and wasm32 checks.
- Run both unmodified Moonraker parsers on the Native, Ares API, CLI, and WASM adapter exports. Check that each parser identifies both producers as `OrcaSlicer` with Native version `2.5.0` and Ares version `Ares-<version>`. Compare all other metadata with the corresponding Native result for that parser except file size, G-code start/end byte offsets, UUID, and modification time. Keep the positive duration and filament checks and the ordered G-code comparison. Before changing the emitter, verify that the legacy parser fails the identity assertion on an Ares export.

## Moonraker compatibility

[Moonraker v0.9.3 `metadata.py:306–324`](https://github.com/Arksine/moonraker/blob/71f9e677b81afcc6b99dd5002f595025c38edc7b/moonraker/components/file_manager/metadata.py#L306-L324) uses `PrusaSlicer.check_identity` to match `OrcaSlicer\s(.*)\son` and takes the capture as `slicer_version`. A hyphen immediately after `OrcaSlicer` prevents that match. [Moonraker `4ba6fd228` `metadata.py:431–456`](https://github.com/Arksine/moonraker/blob/4ba6fd228f264564f6613197fd9abb18ec068cf4/moonraker/components/file_manager/metadata.py#L431-L456) uses `PrusaSlicer.identify` to capture the producer string before the fixed-shape date and time, then splits it at the last space via `rpartition(" ")`. One space after `OrcaSlicer` and none inside `Ares-<version>` agree with both parsers and preserve OrcaSlicer's producer substring.

Supply the unmodified v0.9.3 parser via `ARES_MOONRAKER_LEGACY_METADATA_PY`, alongside `ARES_MOONRAKER_METADATA_PY` for `4ba6fd228`. Verify both against their pinned SHA-256 digests and use the same Python and Pillow suppliers. Call the legacy parser with object rewriting disabled (`extract_metadata(path, False)`) and the newer parser with no processors (`extract_metadata(path, [])`).
